activity_context.topic_title: Improper Integrals of the Second Kind

feedback.problem:
Which of the following is equivalent to 
${\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{\text{d}x}{16-{x}^{2}}?$
feedback.worked_solution:
This is an improper integral of the second kind because the function under the integral is unbounded as we approach the *upper* integration limit from any point that lies in the interval $x\in (0,4):$

$$
f(x)=\frac{1}{16-{x}^{2}}\to \infty \,\text{as}\,x\to {4}^{-}
$$

We can attempt to evaluate this integral by integrating $f(x)$ over the interval $x\in [0,b]$ and taking the limit as $b\to {4}^{-}:$

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{0}^{4}\frac{1}{16-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x & ={lim}_{b\to {4}^{-}}({\int }_{0}^{b}\frac{1}{16-{x}^{2}}\,\text{d}x)\end{aligned}
$$
